images.alt_grc: ὁ Λύσις καὶ ὁ Μικίων ἐκ τοῦ Κεραμεικοῦ βαίνουσιν
images.alt_en: Winter 431/0: Lysis and Mikion walk home from the Kerameikos after the public funeral; ten wagons with cypress coffins, one for each tribe, stand empty by the road.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Δημόκριτος περὶ τοῦ Κλεισθένους λέγει
images.alt_en: Demokritos, the farmer who loves politics, counts off the ten tribes on his fingers for the two boys in a crowded street of the city.
A schematic map of Attica divided into three regions, city, coast and inland, with one 'third' from each joined into a tribe (drawn in the style of a vase painting).
The Council: rows of citizens seated on the benches of the Council house (bouleuterion) listening to a speaker.
images.credit: placeholder (target: reconstruction drawing of the Athenian bouleuterion, CC BY)

images.alt_en: The Monument of the Eponymous Heroes in the Athenian Agora: the long base where the ten tribal heroes stood and public notices were posted.
images.credit: placeholder (target: Wikimedia Commons photograph of the monument's remains, CC BY-SA)

images.alt_grc: ὁ Λύσις ὄστρακον ἐν τῷ ἐργαστηρίῳ εὑρίσκει
images.alt_en: In the workshop yard among heaps of broken pottery, Lysis holds up a sherd with scratched letters; grandfather Kleinias sits on a bench in the sun.

images.alt_grc: ὁ γεωργὸς τῷ Ἀριστείδῃ τὸ ὄστρακον δίδωσιν
images.alt_en: 482 BC in the Agora: a farmer with a hoe on his shoulder hands a potsherd to a quiet, plainly dressed man, Aristides, and asks him to write a name on it.
The Agora fenced off for an ostracism: citizens file in tribe by tribe and drop their sherds; officials count the heap.
Ostraka from the Athenian Agora, 480s BC, inscribed with the names of Themistocles son of Neocles, Aristides son of Lysimachus and others (Agora Museum, Athens).
